title: Landfall and Escarpment
premise: Felix Whitlock, a riverboat captain who has spent five years outrunning a family name he never wanted, is hired to resupply an expedition mapping the headwaters of the Sereno River — until the expedition goes silent and he becomes the only one who can reach them. Following the river into territory his late father once charted and died trying to protect, Felix discovers the missing team, a hidden valley settlement descended from his own bloodline, and proof that his father's disappearance was no accident. To bring anyone home alive, Felix must choose between exposing the valley to the world that will consume it or surrendering the inheritance — the maps, the truth, and the name Whitlock — forever. He burns the charts, carries the survivors downriver, and finally measures his life in years.
about_author: Felix Almeida is a former deckhand turned novelist who spent six seasons working cargo runs on inland waterways before writing full-time. His fiction draws on river lore, expedition diaries, and the quiet stubbornness of people who live by current and weather.

chapters.title: The Sounder's Silence
chapters.summary: POV Felix. On a routine run below Port Calloway, Felix takes a contract from surveyor Imogen Reyes to ferry supplies to her expedition upriver, noting their radio has been dark for nine days. The chapter establishes his rule-bound, mile-counting life and his refusal to discuss his surname. Emotional beat: restless competence masking avoidance.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Loading at the dock, Felix finds his father's old brass compass tucked in the charter paperwork — someone knows who he is. Imogen admits the expedition leader, Dr. Vance, was following charts signed 'E. Whitlock.' Felix nearly walks away, then signs on. Emotional beat: the past catching him at anchor.

chapters.title: First Rapids
chapters.summary: POV Felix. The ascent begins: drowned timber, shifting channels, and a sabotaged marker buoy that nearly wrecks the boat. Felix realizes someone upstream doesn't want traffic. A stowaway boy, Teo, is discovered hiding among crates. Emotional beat: suspicion hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Teo. Through the boy's eyes we learn he fled the valley settlement after seeing strangers taken; he recognizes Felix's compass as 'the finder's mark.' Teo bargains passage home for guidance through the Gorge of Needles. Emotional beat: two runaways recognizing each other.

chapters.title: The Gorge of Needles
chapters.summary: POV Felix. A brutal transit: winching the boat through a slot canyon, losing half their fuel, and finding the expedition's abandoned cache with a radio still warm. Someone from the team is alive and moving ahead of them. Emotional beat: fear sharpened into purpose.

chapters.title: Escarpment
chapters.summary: POV Imogen (journal entries). Flashback chapters reveal what happened at camp: Vance found the valley, the settlers refused exposure, and a faction led by settler matriarch Ada Whitlock — Felix's aunt — sealed the passes. Vance pushed too far and fell. Emotional beat: grief reframing the mission as rescue, not discovery.

chapters.title: The Valley of the Finder
chapters.summary: POV Felix. They reach the hidden valley: terraced farms, descendants of wrecked expeditions, and Ada, who reveals E. Whitlock didn't die mapping — he chose exile here and sent Felix away to keep him out. Two survivors of the expedition are held pending 'the river's judgment.' Emotional beat: inheritance as wound and welcome at once.

chapters.title: Judgment Water
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Flood season arrives early; the dam of logs holding the gorge lake is failing and will drown the valley or erase the lower river towns. Ada insists secrecy above all; Felix argues the valley can only survive by being known on its own terms. The survivors are released into his custody. Emotional beat: conviction over blood loyalty.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Climax: racing the flood, Felix pilots the overloaded boat down the collapsing gorge while Teo and Ada's people breach the logjam in sequence to spare both valley and towns. Ada is lost saving Teo; Felix's charts burn in the spray but the route lives in his hands now. Emotional beat: sacrifice converting inheritance into choice.

chapters.title: Years, Not Miles
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Months later, Felix ferries a small, sanctioned party — not surveyors, but the valley's own envoys — downriver under a treaty Ada drafted in secret. He gives Teo the brass compass and, for the first time, says his full name aloud without flinching. Emotional beat: arrival, identity claimed, the river finally ending somewhere.
